room_or_space: Exterior of the whole house: WEST ELEVATION, EAST ELEVATION and NORTH ELEVATION on one sheet (no interior room shown)

proportions.notable_proportion: No dimensions are written, but the drawing is strongly horizontal: the north elevation is several times wider than it is tall, roofs are low-pitched hipped slabs whose eaves overhang far beyond the wall faces, and the wall planes read as long stacked horizontal bands. The west and east end elevations are comparatively compact, roughly as wide as they are tall.

layout.organisation: Three exterior elevations: west and east side by side in the upper half, the long north elevation across the lower half, scale note and bar scale lower right. The building is drawn as stepped horizontal tiers: a long main block under a broad hipped roof slab, a smaller set-back upper storey block under its own hipped roof, a tall rectangular chimney rising above it, and low garden/terrace walls with copings extending the base outward on the west and north sides.
layout.axes: A dominant horizontal axis runs the length of the north elevation; the upper storey block and chimney make an off-centre vertical accent rather than a centred one. No elevation is bilaterally symmetrical; masses step down from the upper block toward the ends. The west and east elevations show the short end of the same stepped composition, with a secondary hipped roof over a projecting main-level bay in front of the taller block.
layout.entry_sequence: No principal entrance is marked. The north elevation shows a single ground-level door with a small light above it at the base of the central block, beside runs of low windows; the west elevation shows full-height glazed openings between piers under the small hipped roof, opening onto a walled terrace. No entrance steps, path, porch roof or canopy is drawn.
layout.circulation: Not shown (elevations only). Low walls, piers and a raised terrace parapet with planter bowls indicate walled terraces at the west end and along the north base; the ground line, drawn with grass hatching, falls away toward the west end of the north elevation and steps down at the right of the west elevation. No stairs are drawn.

details: Deeply overhanging low-pitched hipped roofs drawn as thin slabs projecting well beyond the wall faces, with a thin layered fascia, on every mass
Continuous horizontal banding: brick wall planes with fine horizontal hatching capped by plain coping/sill courses that run uninterrupted along walls, parapets and garden walls
Repeated tall narrow casement windows with geometric leaded glazing (paired diagonals forming chevrons/diamonds), grouped in bands between slender piers under the eaves

Stepped massing with an upper storey block and tall rectangular chimney rising above the main roof, and shallow planter bowls set on the terrace parapets
